## Remove redundant phrasing

Screen readers already announce an image. Begin with its meaning instead of phrases such as “image of.”

<KnowledgeCheck
  id="knowledge-check-write-concise-alt-text"
  type="multiple"
  prompt="Which revisions remove redundant wording without removing meaning?"
  outcomes={["write-concise-alt-text"]}
  options={[
    {
      id: "remove-image-of",
      text: "Remove “image of” from “Image of a warning sign”",
      feedback: "Screen readers already announce the image, so this phrase repeats information.",
    },
    {
      id: "keep-warning",
      text: "Keep the words “warning sign”",
      feedback: "Those words communicate the image's meaning and should remain.",
    },
    {
      id: "remove-warning",
      text: "Remove the word “warning”",
      feedback: "Removing “warning” would discard the sign's purpose rather than remove redundancy.",
    },
  ]}
  answer={["remove-image-of", "keep-warning"]}
  explanation="Concise alternative text removes wording already supplied by the interface while preserving the image's purpose."
/>

<PracticeTask
  id="practice-task-write-concise-alt-text"
  title="Polish an optional description"
  level="stretch"
  estimatedMinutes={5}
  goal="Make a useful description shorter without losing its purpose"
  outcomes={["write-concise-alt-text"]}
  criteria={["The revision removes redundancy and preserves the warning"]}
>
  Revise “Image of a warning sign beside the publish button.”

  <TaskSolution
    reasoning="The interface already announces the image, while the warning and its location carry useful meaning."
    alternatives={["Warning sign beside the publish button."]}
    likelyErrors={["Removing the warning together with the redundant opening phrase."]}
  />
</PracticeTask>
